Checks: Agent Merge repairs, waits for and merges on the checks that count (`classifyRequiredPullRequestChecks`): required checks, the jobs an unfinished required check `needs:` (so a failed job of an aggregate gate such as `PR Gate` is repaired before the gate even reports), and every check when the base branch requires none. A failed check suite that has not reported a check, which only counts in that last case, such as a workflow that failed to start, is repaired like any failed check, as Fix CI does; `readAgentMergeCI` reports that it has no logs or annotations. In that last case, while GitHub refuses to list the head's check suites, the checks stay pending, as a suite that has not reported may still fail: Agent Merge neither marks a draft ready nor merges, but still repairs the known failures. A workflow rerun deferred until its run finishes also covers the failure of the required check that waits for the deferred jobs, which only reports once they finish, until the rerun is requested. Whether a draft is ready for review (`agentMergeReadyForReview`, which hands the primary button back to Mark Ready) leaves out the check names matching `chat.artifactIntegrations.githubPullRequests.autoMarkReadyIgnoredChecks`: the folder's workspace value, which the client mirrors into `readyIgnoredChecks` when it writes the folder's settings, when the setting changes, and when it sees a folder enabled without one; otherwise the user's value mirrored to the host.

GitHub expires that page after an hour, so a fresh notice follows only if the folder is still blocked by then. The checks section is shown for open and draft PRs, but omitted for closed and merged PRs. All loaded checks, including optional checks, remain visible. Only the checks that count (see Required checks below) need a repair: they decide Fix CI, the needs-repair PR icon, Mark Ready and Merge.
